title: OpenAI Chat Completions semantic shim and response resynthesis for Redwood API compatibility
creator: Priya Nair
description: Implement a semantic-level compatibility shim that maps OpenAI Chat Completions (CC) request/response semantics to Redwood's canonical API shape without changing client-visible behavior. The shim must handle request normalization (roles, name fields, user metadata), function/tool calling semantics, streaming deltas vs final chunks, structured output coercion, and edge-cases in OpenAI payloads so Redwood hosted and private runtimes can accept OA-CC clients with minimal customer changes.
background: Multiple customers have requested the ability to point existing OpenAI Chat Completions SDKs at Redwood endpoints. Previous engineering tickets focused on wire-level translators and event framers; this work targets a semantic layer that reconciles differences in: (1) function_call signals, including explicit name vs. object returns, (2) streaming delta semantics and how tool-invocation frames are emitted, (3) structured outputs when OA returns content with embedded JSON or tool results, and (4) legacy fields like stop, n, and logit_bias. Goal is minimal surprise for OA clients while preserving Redwood runtime telemetry and SLOs.
goals: Normalize incoming OA-CC requests to Redwood canonical request model (messages, model, temperature, top_p, max_tokens -> token_budget)
Translate OA function_call instructions into Redwood tool-invoke intent + preserve original function metadata in telemetry
Support streaming delta frames from runtime and re-synthesize OA-compatible SSE events (delta, done, tool_call)
Ensure structured output responses (JSON blobs, tool results) are returned with OA-compatible fields and consistent ids
Provide comprehensive integration tests and a staged rollout plan with canary enabled for OA-compat endpoints
acceptance_criteria: OA-CC requests (roles, names, user metadata) accepted by Redwood endpoints and round-tripped back in responses where expected
Function/tool calling: when OA client supplies function definitions + function_call: 'auto'/'none'/explicit name behave identically to OA baseline for a suite of 12 function patterns
Streaming: clients using OA SSE semantics receive delta events with the same incremental tokens and final 'DONE' event; no extra buffering-induced reordering beyond 50ms target
Structured outputs: JSON-first content is emitted as text+metadata such that OA clients using naive JSON.parse(body) succeed for >=95% of test prompts
No regression in per-token latency 99p when enabling OA-CC compatibility routes (within 10% of non-compat baseline)
technical_notes: Request normalizer components live in runtime/proxy/compat/semantic_shim.go
Canonical mapping rules: messages -> canonical_segments; OA 'name' field maps to Redwood message.originator; 'user' props appended to metadata.headers.user_id

Function calling mapping: OA function list -> Redwood ToolDescriptors; preserve OA function.json_schema as tool.output_schema; explicit function_call.name triggers immediate tool-invoke event and halts token generation

Streaming conversion: runtime produces Redwood streaming frames (token, kv_hint, tool_invocation_start, tool_invocation_chunk, end). Shim will convert these to OA SSE frames: data: {"delta": {...}} / data: [DONE] semantics

Resynthesis: where OA expects a single message with content and a function call object, the shim will synthesize that object from tool invocation outputs and attach the same 'name' and 'arguments' fields OA clients expect
Edge cases: logit_bias is validated and clamped to supported tokens; unknown token ids are ignored with a telemetry warning; negative max_tokens -> treated as error with OA-compatible 400 response
Telemetry: preserve original OA request_id header in traces and emit compat.mapping_version label for A/B experiments
Security: do not surface internal Redwood tool execution traces to OA clients; only sanitized tool outputs are passed through
progress_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike completed. Validated that OA function_call: 'auto' semantics can be implemented by deferring to the runtime's tool-ranking component. Notes in confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/CC-compat-spike

2025-02-25: Initial PR with request normalizer & unit tests opened (github.com/redwood/re-runtime PR #7542). Basic mapping for message.role/name/user implemented. Review feedback from @sofia-alvarez: add explicit tests for multi-name collisions.

2025-03-01: Streaming shim implemented in proxy layer; integration test harness that replays recorded OA SSE streams added (tests/compat/oa_stream_replay). Initial perf shows 7% tail-latency increase under synthetic load.
2025-03-04: Function-call resynthesis logic complete; end-to-end test with runtime tool mock passes. Filed follow-up ENG-602010 to tighten tool output sanitization for PII-sensitive functions
2025-03-05: Landed second PR that adds telemetry tags and feature flag (compat-oa-cc) behind runtime flag for controlled rollout. QA starting canary 1 (10% traffic) tomorrow. PRs: #7542, #7620
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Streaming conversion may introduce extra copies of token payloads increasing CPU. Mitigation: zero-copy buffer slices where possible and opt-in compat flag to measure cost before full rollout.
Risk: Function-call resynthesis may leak internal tool names or schemas. Mitigation: enforce allowlist + sanitizer; require security review for high-risk tool descriptors.

Risk: Clients depending on OA-specific timing or chunk counts may observe behavioral differences. Mitigation: document differences clearly and offer advisory deprecation window for customers with tight coupling.

Risk: Mismatch in stop / max_tokens semantics causing truncated replies. Mitigation: perform exhaustive fuzz tests and add safety-net: runtime will fallback to forced end-of-stream with OA 400 if client-visible inconsistency detected
test_plan: Unit tests: request normalizer permutations (role/name/user, missing fields, malformed logit_bias)
Integration: run recorded OA session replays against compat shim and assert event sequence & reconstructed messages
E2E: instrumented QA job that runs 50K OA-compat requests across models and checks functional parity with OA baseline harness
Performance: A/B bench comparing compat-flag on vs off under 1k rps for 10m windows; capture token-level CPU and 99p latency
Security: run static analysis + manual review for function schema sanitization; coordinate with security on a checklist
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Feature flag rollout to internal customers and staging (compat-oa-cc = true). Monitor tool-invocation metrics and error rates for 48h
Phase 2: Canary 10% traffic in hosted region us-west1 for 72h if metrics stable
Phase 3: 50% traffic and gradual enable for dedicated clusters with opt-in via customer console
Phase 4: Full global rollout and documentation update; deprecate old wire-level proxy after 60 days
